themes_detail.label: Park Safety & Wildlife Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Park rule violations spiked to 6 complaints this week versus a 1.0 weekly average—a 500% increase (z-score: 7.07)—while animal complaints in parks jumped to 13 this week from a 2.9 weekly average, a 352% spike (z-score: 6.59), suggesting a sudden loss of park management or wildlife control this week.
evidence: Violation of Park Rules: 6 complaints this week vs. 1.0 weekly average (500% increase, z-score: 7.07)
Animal in a Park: 13 complaints this week vs. 2.9 weekly average (352% increase, z-score: 6.59)
Both spikes occurred in same week, suggesting systemic park management failure
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Department about sudden spike in park violations and animal incidents—what triggered this?
Survey residents in Central Park/Riverside Park areas about what rule-breaking or animal encounters they've witnessed this week

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes Flooding Streets
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints surged to 4 this week from a 0.8 weekly average—a 433% spike (z-score: 3.92)—indicating rapid deterioration of bike-share or personal bike abandonment across the district this week.
evidence: Abandoned Bike complaints: 4 this week vs. 0.8 weekly average (433% increase, z-score: 3.92)
Spike is isolated to this week with no prior acceleration pattern
Complements broader street condition complaints (1,064 total over 90 days)
reporting_angles: Contact Citi Bike and NYPD about any system issues or enforcement sweeps this week
Walk key neighborhoods to photograph and map abandoned bike clusters—are they concentrated in specific areas?

themes_detail.label: Building Exterior Hazards Jump
themes_detail.summary: Complaints about items outside buildings spiked to 4 this week from a 0.5 weekly average—a 700% increase (z-score: 7.0)—suggesting new facade deterioration, debris, or safety hazards on building exteriors this week.
evidence: OUTSIDE BUILDING complaints: 4 this week vs. 0.5 weekly average (700% increase, z-score: 7.0)
High z-score (7.0) indicates statistically extreme deviation from 8-week baseline
1,225 total building permits filed in last 90 days, including 7 full demolitions—potential trigger for exterior hazards
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 complaints with DOB permit filings to identify which buildings are generating complaints
Contact Buildings Department to learn if there's been a spike in facade inspection violations or debris citations

themes_detail.label: Day Care Quality Concerns (Earlier Trend)
themes_detail.summary: Day care complaints hit 3 two weeks ago versus a 0.4 weekly average—a 700% increase (z-score: 3.77)—though this spike occurred 2 weeks ago rather than this week, it remains the most severe sustained deviation in the child care space.
evidence: Day Care complaints: 3 two weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% increase, z-score: 3.77)
Timing is 2 weeks old, not this week, but represents significant concern for child safety/quality
Aligns with community board's repeated requests for educational programs and health services expansion
reporting_angles: FOIA request to Department of Health for any day care inspection violations filed in past 2 weeks on Upper West Side
Interview parents at affected centers about what triggered complaints—safety, staffing, conditions?

themes_detail.label: Lost Property Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Lost property complaints increased to 13 last week from an 8.0 weekly average—a 62% increase (z-score: 3.33)—potentially signaling increased foot traffic, tourism (post-Japan Parade), or organized theft last week.
evidence: Lost Property complaints: 13 last week vs. 8.0 weekly average (62% increase, z-score: 3.33)
Japan Parade occurred 2026-05-13 (recently mentioned in local news), which could have driven visitor-related lost items
Pattern may be event-driven rather than indicating systemic issue
reporting_angles: Analyze if lost property spike correlates with Japan Parade attendance last week
Check if NYPD precinct data shows corresponding uptick in larceny or theft reports
